title: Algy
html_source:
Algernon Charles Swinburne (1837-1909) was an avant-garde poet and appears to be admired by Mulligan and maybe Stephen as well. In Chapter 1 – Telemachus, Mulligan quotes from two of Swinburne’s poems.

ACCEPTED SUGGESTION: It is no coincidence that Joyce has shortened the poet’s name thusly and chosen to mention him in this paragraph. Joyce by referring to the poet Algy, cleverly complements the visual modality of the seascape he is describing viscerally and euphonically. Algy sounds similar to algae, there are but two letters difference. This reference therefore sits harmoniously with Joyce’s previous descriptions of types of seaweed.
